tasks.prompt: I just need the raw contents of one file in my terminal. What command should I run?
Before installing anything on Debian, how can I search package names and descriptions for "ripgrep"?
On macOS, find a file by its name through Spotlight's index; I know the filename but not its folder.
On Windows, find files by their filename pattern recursively, while excluding hidden directories.
In this directory tree, list matching file paths ordered by their total size, largest first.
What command shows me the status of the named systemd service "nginx"?
On macOS, use Spotlight to find items containing "quarterly report", but restrict results to ~/Documents.
In PowerShell, list the items under D:\Projects rather than the current folder.
Show the amount of disk space consumed by ~/Downloads itself, excluding the filesystem's other directories.
Show only the journal entries for nginx that were emitted while its service was active, and follow them until it stops.
On macOS, use the search index to find files whose contents mention "invoice overdue".
Find the phrase "connection refused" across files in this Windows folder, ignoring letter case.
Search this log with an extended regular expression, without regard to letter case.
On Debian, list only installed packages matching a regular expression and sort them by installation date.
Use Spotlight to return PDFs whose text contains both "budget" and "approved", modified in the past seven days.
For a quick inventory, print just the names of the current folder's contents, with no details.
From a file, show only the substring that matched the search, not the full matching line.
Show the network interfaces in brief link-layer form, rather than their full details.
Use Spotlight to list matching paths and include a total match count on the first line.
List only the first ten filenames from this folder, without any headings or metadata.
Concatenate these two files into a new output file, leaving the inputs untouched.
I need to edit a systemd unit file for a service; what command opens that unit file for editing?
Capture only the currently selected macOS window directly into the clipboard as a PNG.
On Windows, move a file into a destination directory and create the directory if it doesn't exist.
Copy a directory tree while preserving symbolic links, and replace existing destination files without prompting.
Remove a Debian package but leave its configuration files on the machine.
Open a new instance of a Mac application by its bundle identifier, even if another instance is running.
Move a Windows file over an existing file, keeping a backup copy of the old version automatically.
Copy a file with common cp, show a diff, and ask before writing the changes.
On Debian, remove a package only if no running service depends on it, and explain which services would be affected first.
Reveal this file in Finder without opening it: ~/Desktop/notes.txt.
Show me the contents of the current Windows directory.
Using common sed, replace matching text in the original file itself and leave a backup copy.
Before enabling the nginx service at boot, preview every unit and dependency that would change.
On a Mac, check whether "Safari" is already running and launch it only when it is not.
In Windows Command Prompt, list the directory sorted by date and time with the oldest entries first.
Sort these values numerically rather than alphabetically, so 10 comes after 2.
For one systemd service, show journal entries in chronological order with timestamps converted to my local timezone.
After a five-second delay, record a screen video at 30 frames per second with audio.
List files newest-first, grouped with directories first, and only those changed today.
Sort these lines case-insensitively so that capitalization doesn't affect their order.
Show memory usage in human-readable units like MB or GB.
Have my Mac speak this phrase using a chosen voice and a specified speaking rate.
On Windows, list file sizes in human-readable IEC units and emit the result as JSON.
Print each line with its line number and colorize the filename using the common cat command.
Follow the latest 25 system journal entries and keep displaying new messages as they arrive.
Read the current macOS clipboard and pass its contents to grep to find "TODO".
Filter a Windows command's piped output by three phrases in order, then print only the match count.
Write standard input to a new common-platform file only if that file does not already exist, doing it atomically.
Pipe journal entries through a filter that redacts IP addresses before showing them.
Launch the macOS app registered under bundle identifier com.apple.Safari.
Rename a Windows file to a new name on the same drive, where that destination name doesn't already exist.
Copy a file and preserve its full source path beneath the destination, creating intermediate directories as needed.
Restart the named systemd service only if it has failed, and record the previous state.
Reveal an app's bundle identifier for an already-running Mac application without launching another copy.
In PowerShell, include hidden items in the listing for the current directory.
Find files modified today and run a command once for each matching file.
Show filesystem usage in human-readable form with inode counts, but include only mounts above 90% full.
Record a screen video that includes the mouse cursor and save a separate audio track.
Recursively list only hidden Windows files modified today that are larger than 1 MB.
